outlier.evidence: Ratings span 7 to 8. Reviewer_Kz6Q's lone 8 is one point above the others and is backed by a substantive 8-hour review with three specific questions, so it is not an outlier.

inattentive_reviews.evidence: 3 hours, confidence 3 with 'Math/other details were not carefully checked', one paragraph of summary and praise plus a single question, no reply to the rebuttal. Its 7 is weak evidence either way, although the one question (unbounded logistic minimizer) is informed.

checkable_claims.claim: Definition 4: for Tikhonov the qualification should be q = 1, not 1/2.
checkable_claims.evidence: The authors conceded this in committee B on 2021-08-18 ('Tikhonov has qualification of 1, and not 1/2 as incorrectly stated'); camera-ready p.5 reads 'has qualification 1'. In A the authors answered with a notation argument they later withdrew, and CRtT did not follow up. Checked against a/paper.pdf, which is the camera-ready, not the submission.

checkable_claims.claim: Supplement Assumption 9 has a lower bound on df_λ that the main-paper capacity condition lacks.
checkable_claims.evidence: Authors: 'This is a typo which will be corrected'. Camera-ready Assumption 4 (p.4) now states s λ^{-1/α} ≤ df_λ ≤ S λ^{-1/α}.

checkable_claims.claim: Theorem 1 hides how its constants depend on t, so it seems to give good rates even as t → ∞, where the estimator is unregularized.
checkable_claims.evidence: A presentation gap, not an error: C_var grows linearly in t (authors' reply, appendix Eq. 55). The camera-ready adds an 'Influence of t' paragraph on p.6.

checkable_claims.claim: For the logistic loss the risk minimizer ln(η/(1−η)) is usually unbounded, but the analysis seems to need a bounded θ*.
checkable_claims.evidence: Assumption 2 (p.3) requires θ* ∈ H, which with a bounded kernel makes θ* bounded. The authors agreed and deferred the L² case to future work; the camera-ready adds a sentence saying so before Assumption 2.

checkable_claims.claim: The paper does not contrast its guarantees directly with Marteau-Ferey et al., and the gain looks incremental.
checkable_claims.evidence: The authors agreed and promised a comparison; the camera-ready adds 'Example: a very easy learning task' on p.6 (Tikhonov n^{-2/3} against iterated Tikhonov n^{-20/21}). Sec. 3.1 says the proof builds 'upon the tools from [1]'. Whether that is incremental is a judgment; B's Reviewer_r7mh saw the same fact and called it a small issue.

rebuttal.evidence: Reviewer_rN14 edited the review on 2021-08-18: 'I appreciate the added clarity in differentiating from Marteau-Ferey et al. [1], and so I have adjusted my score accordingly' (final 7; the earlier value is not exposed). Reviewer_Kz6Q on 2021-09-10: 'I will keep my score as it is'. Reviewer_CRtT and Reviewer_xAhK did not edit or reply.
rebuttal.what_convinced_or_not: The explicit rate comparison (Marteau-Ferey's error stops at n^{-2/3} with α = 1; iterated Tikhonov reaches n^{-(2r+1)/(2r+2)}) convinced rN14. CRtT's qualification question got the authors' 'different notation' answer, which they withdrew in committee B; in A that answer stood unchallenged.

ac.evidence: Three sentences: 'All reviewers agree that the paper is technically quite interesting and well-executed', 'a nice contribution to the conference program', and a request to add the Marteau-Ferey comparison that cleared up 'some confusions'. Poster matches the 7.25 mean; nothing argues for or against a spotlight.

main_reasons_for_decision: Three 7s and one 8 (mean 7.25): a consensus of 'good paper, accept', not 'top 50%'.
The three 7-reviewers praised soundness and clarity but did not argue significance; only Kz6Q called the contribution significant.
Novelty over Marteau-Ferey et al. was the live question; rN14 reached 7 only after the rebuttal's rate comparison.
The AC followed the consensus with no argument about the tier.

outlier.evidence: Final ratings span 7 to 8. Reviewer_v7Aq was a detractor before the rebuttal ('temporarily holding a weak reject') on a correct, checkable point (Tikhonov's qualification), and moved to 7 once the authors conceded it; no outlier remains.

inattentive_reviews.evidence: 8 at confidence 5 ('checked the math/other details carefully') with 5 hours and a six-sentence main review of praise, no technical criticism and no sign of a math check. It did not mention the qualification error that CRtT and v7Aq found. Discussion reply: 'would like to keep my rating'. The limitations note on confidence dependence is expert, but the 8 is weak evidence of quality.

checkable_claims.evidence: Authors conceded on 2021-08-18 and showed the error stays outside the proofs; camera-ready p.5 reads 'qualification 1'. The same camera-ready paragraph still gives wrong saturated rates (n^{-α(1+2q)/(1+α(1+2q))}, and n^{-α/(1+α)} for Tikhonov), which contradict Theorem 1, Table 1 (t = 1 theory 0.80 = 2α/(1+2α) at α = 2) and the authors' own corrected text (n^{-2αq/(1+2αq)}).

checkable_claims.claim: Assumption 1 uses the Hessian before it is defined; it should read Tr ∇²ℓ_z(0).
checkable_claims.evidence: Authors: 'Indeed, this should read Tr ∇²ℓ_z(0)'. Camera-ready Assumption 1 (p.3) now reads so.

checkable_claims.claim: The assumptions (self-concordance, source, capacity) and the self-concordant Taylor bounds come from Marteau-Ferey et al. and Bach; the work is an iterative improvement.
checkable_claims.evidence: Camera-ready: Assumption 1 is 'also introduced in [1]'; the bound in Eq. (13) 'first appeared in [11] and was given in this form in [1]'; Sec. 3.1 builds 'upon the tools from [1]'. r7mh still called this a small issue and gave 8.

checkable_claims.claim: Optimal rates need t ≥ r + 1/2 iterations.
checkable_claims.evidence: Theorem 1 (p.5): the rate in Eq. (11) holds when 't ≥ r + 1/2'. This is the only specific statement in KRE1's main review.

rebuttal.evidence: Reviewer_v7Aq: 'I am temporarily holding a weak reject', then a post-rebuttal note (edited 2021-08-18): 'I am therefore happy to vote for acceptance'; final 7. Reviewer_r7mh edited on 2021-08-28 to add 'This is a strong paper'; whether its 8 changed is not recorded. Reviewer_7njB (2021-08-22) and Reviewer_KRE1 (2021-08-27) kept 8.
rebuttal.what_convinced_or_not: v7Aq rejected the first 'different notation' answer and asked again on 2021-08-13. The second answer conceded that line 153 was wrong and showed the final rates are unaffected; that concession moved v7Aq. r7mh accepted the proposed paragraph on the source and capacity conditions.

ac.evidence: The meta-review summarizes Theorem 1, Proposition 2 and the synthetic experiments, frames the work as answering whether iterated Tikhonov overcomes the saturation of [1], then says 'The reviewers agreed that the authors deliver a solid theoretical contribution ... of clear interest to the NeurIPS audience'. Spotlight matches the 7.75 mean; the only tier-relevant phrase is the broad-interest claim about kernel methods.

main_reasons_for_decision: Reviewers called the result significant (KRE1, 7njB) and the paper strong (r7mh).
The only detractor, v7Aq, moved from weak reject to 7 once the qualification error was conceded as a typo outside the proofs.
The AC framed the work as answering the saturation question left by Marteau-Ferey et al., of clear interest given how widely kernel methods are used.

issues_only_a: No explicit rate comparison with Marteau-Ferey et al. (Reviewer_rN14)
Dependence of Theorem 1's constants on t, and behaviour as t → ∞ (Reviewer_CRtT)
Supplement and main text disagree on the capacity condition's lower bound (Reviewer_CRtT)
How to choose t in practice (Reviewer_Kz6Q)
Effect of the dimension of Y (Reviewer_Kz6Q)
Other definitions of generalized self-concordance and a missing ball-oracle reference (Reviewer_rN14)
issues_only_b: Newton-based inner solvers scale poorly; first-order solvers not discussed (Reviewer_v7Aq)
Unknown dependence of the bounds on the confidence level δ (Reviewer_KRE1)
Missing link to sequential greedy approximation (Reviewer_7njB)
Assumption 1 uses the Hessian before its definition; overloaded symbols (Reviewer_7njB)
Little intuition for the source and capacity conditions (Reviewer_r7mh)
Eq. (19) and the function L̄ are hard to interpret (Reviewer_v7Aq)
shared_issues: Tikhonov's qualification printed as 1/2 instead of 1 (Reviewer_CRtT in A, Reviewer_v7Aq in B); the authors conceded it only in B
Incremental over Marteau-Ferey et al.: same assumptions and self-concordance toolbox (Reviewer_rN14 in A, Reviewer_r7mh in B)
Minimizer assumed to lie in H, which excludes unbounded or non-attainable targets (Reviewer_xAhK and Reviewer_Kz6Q in A, Reviewer_KRE1 in B)
Dense notation in the self-concordance definition (Reviewer_CRtT in A, Reviewer_7njB in B)
Experiments only on toy synthetic data, treated as adequate by both (Reviewer_Kz6Q in A, Reviewer_r7mh in B)
verdict: The spotlight/poster split is score calibration, not substance. Both committees saw a sound, clearly written extension of Marteau-Ferey et al.'s Tikhonov analysis for generalized self-concordant losses to iterated Tikhonov, which removes saturation and reaches optimal rates; both noted modest novelty and dense notation, and neither found a flaw in the results. The one real error, Tikhonov's qualification printed as 1/2 instead of 1, was raised in both committees (Reviewer_CRtT in A, Reviewer_v7Aq in B) and sits in background prose, not in the theorems. Three of A's reviewers chose 7 and three of B's chose 8 for similar assessments, giving means of 7.25 and 7.75, and each AC's short meta-review follows its mean without arguing the tier. The visible weighting difference is novelty: A's Reviewer_rN14 called the gain over Marteau-Ferey 'somewhat incremental' and A's AC made that comparison its only specific request, while B's Reviewer_r7mh made the same observation, called it a small issue, and framed the result as the answer to an open question from Marteau-Ferey et al., a framing B's AC repeated. B's higher mean also rests partly on thin support: Reviewer_KRE1's 8 at confidence 5 comes with a brief, uncritical review, and Reviewer_r7mh's 8 carries confidence 2.
